daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo is expected to convene party leaders again to discuss selection of a replacement vice president, while the MPR has established three working groups to prepare for the selection process. Former Vice President Jusuf Kalla commented that the replacement must be smart, and former Chief Security Minister Mahfud MD warned of potential new political problems if the vice president is inaugurated on 9 December. Political observers are debating whether loyalty alone is sufficient for Ring 1 positions around Prabowo, with calls for a technocrat vice president gaining traction.

  • DPR Deputy Speaker Dasco invited schools and victims' families to participate in revision of the Child Protection Law.
  • PSI Secretary General Abang Ijo Hapidin stated after meeting Jokowi in Solo that PSI is not in opposition.
  • The Ministry of Home Affairs awarded high-performing local governments in the Maluku-Nusa Tenggara region to strengthen regional competitiveness.
  • Police postponed a press conference on a treason case after raiding homes linked to Brigadier General Tedjo Kusumo and Police Commissioner Imanudin, with one house in Bogor allegedly used as a treason coordination post.
  • The Secretary of Karawang district strengthened oversight of the digital village head elections in 2026.
  • Religious Affairs Minister Yaqut testified in his corruption trial, calling it a jihad, while denying receiving $71,000 and admitting he assigned Gus Alex coordination tasks in hajj administration.
  • The Bengkulu Police Chief, Inspector General Yudhi Sulistianto, made headlines after prostrating to apologize to students.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia was elected to the ICAO Council for the 2026–2028 term, securing a seat on the International Civil Aviation Organization's governing body. The government also plans to revise the State Defense Law in 2027 to strengthen legal frameworks for national security. At the APEC summit, President Prabowo held bilateral meetings with Putin and Xi Jinping, securing investment commitments worth Rp 1,600 trillion.

  • Indonesia and Qatar discussed additional direct flights to Bali to boost tourism connectivity.
  • Indonesia and the European Union finalized IEU-CEPA preparations ahead of signing, with Coordinating Minister Airlangga discussing accelerated implementation with the EU.
  • The Indonesian Navy tested combat readiness of Ranai Naval Base personnel.
  • Indonesia called for more blue economy investment in Southeast Asia during a regional forum.

Other

The government's free meal program has reached 58 million recipients, with the BGN (Badan Gizi Nasional) accelerating expansion. In a new policy shift, BGN announced that elite schools will no longer receive free meal benefits, with resources redirected to schools in disadvantaged, frontier, and outermost (3T) regions. The government's MBG 2.0 administrative reforms have generated Rp44 trillion in budget savings.

  • Labor leader Said Iqbal demanded Jakarta Governor revise the 2027 provincial minimum wage to Rp 6.21 million, up from the announced Rp 6.13 million.
  • Indonesia's gas supply to Singapore, which had been curtailed, has returned to normal.
  • PLN signed six power purchase agreements at COP31 climate conference.
  • The Price Control Task Force revoked PT RAPP's permit, with 338,536 hectares of forest returning to state control, and also found a palm oil mill in Riau allegedly processing fruit from illegal plantations.
  • The KPK questioned former national team manager Endri Erawan in a money laundering case involving a former Kutai Kartanegara regent.
